html:
The Illyrian Provinces were a part of the French Empire on the east coast of the Adriatic and inland, created by Napoleon in 1809 with its capital at Ljubljana.

Austria had to cede the lands after its defeat in 1809. The French brought their law code, ended many feudal dues, built roads and opened schools that taught in Slovene and Croatian alongside French. The name revived the old Roman province of Illyria and later inspired the Illyrian movement of South Slav unity. Austria took the lands back in 1813. The episode lasted four years but gave Slovene intellectuals their first taste of their language in public life, and the poet Valentin Vodnik wrote an ode to it.
sum: The Illyrian Provinces were a part of the French Empire on the east coast of the Adriatic and inland, created by Napoleon in 1809 with its capital at Ljubljana.
